subject: set all text in theme to serif?

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: set all text in theme to serif?
parts:
Silly question:

I see how I can set the family of individual text elements to
theme_text(family="serif"), and I can hack the following to get all
text in a plot set in a serif font:

> text_elements <- grep("title|text",names(theme_get()),value=TRUE)
> theme_orig <- theme_get()[text_elements]
> theme_new <- lapply(theme_orig,function(x) theme_text(family="serif"))
> do.call(theme_update,theme_new)

is there a simpler/easier/more elegant way to do this?

Ben Bolker

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: set all text in theme to serif?
parts:
This is also a hack and probably ill-advised. Also, I doubt that it is
simpler, easier, or more elegant. But I spent some time figuring it
out, so I thought I would share.

library(ggplot2)
d <- data.frame(x=runif(10),y=runif(10))
g1 <- ggplot(d,aes(x=x,y=y))+geom_point() + ylab("This is the Y-Axis
Label") + xlab("This is the X-Axis Label")

g1 + theme_grey()

formals(theme_text)$family <- "serif"
assignInNamespace("theme_text", theme_text, "ggplot2")

dev.new()
g1 + theme_grey()


Best,
Ista
